Data Sourcing and Generation Steps:

1. CLONE / SYNC THE ORE ENGINE SOURCE
   Source: OreStudio's fork of the ORE Engine, kept in sync with
   upstream OpenSourceRisk/Engine.
     git@github.com:OreStudio/Engine.git    (fork, push target)
     git@github.com:OpenSourceRisk/Engine.git   (upstream, pull-only)
   Kept as a separate checkout OUTSIDE this repo (e.g.
   ~/Development/ORE/Engine), not a submodule -- it's a multi-gigabyte
   C++ source tree (QuantLib + QuantExt + OREData + OREAnalytics) that
   only needs to exist locally when actually rebuilding a package; this
   repo only vendors the resulting binary artefact.
   Commands (first time):
     git clone --recurse-submodules git@github.com:OreStudio/Engine.git
     cd Engine
     git remote add upstream git@github.com:OpenSourceRisk/Engine.git
   Commands (updating the fork before building):
     git fetch upstream
     git checkout master && git merge --ff-only upstream/master
     git submodule update --init --recursive
     git push origin master

2. BUILD
   Preset: linux-clang-ninja-release (CMakePresets.json; requires Boost
   >= 1.75.0 -- BOOST_ROOT=/usr picks up the system apt package, e.g.
   libboost-all-dev, no separate Boost build needed).
   Commands:
     BOOST=/usr cmake --preset linux-clang-ninja-release
     cmake --build build/linux-clang-ninja-release -j <nproc>
   Target: build/linux-clang-ninja-release/App/ore (the CLI executable)
   plus libOREAnalytics.so/libOREData.so/libQuantExt.so/
   libQuantLib.so.1 it links against. This step alone leaves the
   executable's RPATH pointing at absolute paths inside the build tree
   (readelf -d App/ore | grep RUNPATH) -- not portable, fixed in the
   next step.

3. PACKAGE
   Script: external/ore/tools/package_ore.sh
   Command:
     external/ore/tools/package_ore.sh <path-to-build-dir>
   What it does (see the script's own header comment for full detail):
     a. Copies App/ore plus every shared library `ldd` reports it needs,
        EXCLUDING glibc/loader/libgcc (linux-vdso, ld-linux, libc,
        libm, libpthread, libdl, librt -- those must always come from
        the host) -- into a flat package dir with a lib/ subdirectory.
     b. Rewrites RPATH via patchelf: $ORIGIN/lib on the executable,
        $ORIGIN on every bundled library -- so the package finds its
        own bundled libraries wherever it's extracted, with zero
        environment setup (matches how ores.compute.wrapper actually
        spawns the engine -- see
        projects/ores.compute/wrapper/src/app/application.cpp, no
        LD_LIBRARY_PATH customisation).
     c. Writes manifest.json ({"executable": ..., "args": ["Input/ore.xml"]}) --
        the minimal, wrapper-consumed manifest. Deliberately unversioned
        prose-free; see this directory's own manifest.json for the
        human-facing provenance record instead.
     d. tars the whole package dir into ore-<version>-x64-linux.tar.gz.
   Version: by default, `git describe --tags --always` (leading 'v'
   stripped) against the build dir's own source tree, auto-discovered
   from CMakeCache.txt's CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY -- override with
   --version if a different string is wanted.

4. VERIFY (self-test, on by default)
   The same script run then:
     a. Confirms the packaged executable's `ldd` output resolves every
        dependency inside the package itself, with NO path pointing
        back into the build tree -- proves the RPATH rewrite actually
        worked, not just that it was attempted.
     b. Extracts external/ore/packages/TA002_IR_Swap.tar.gz (a plain
        20Y EUR fixed-vs-float IR swap -- see that file's own entry in
        this directory's manifest.json) into a scratch job directory
        and runs the packaged executable against it exactly the way
        ores.compute.wrapper does: `<exe> Input/ore.xml` with the job
        directory as cwd.
     c. Tolerantly diffs every Output/*.csv against
        external/ore/examples/Academy/TA002_IR_Swap/ExpectedOutput/ --
        see external/ore/tools/compare_csv.py's own doc for why this is
        NOT a byte-exact diff (cross-compiler/library floating-point
        noise in the last 1-2 significant digits is expected and not a
        defect; a newer engine legitimately adding trailing report
        columns an older reference doesn't have is also not a defect).
     d. Writes a sign-off report,
        <package>.diff-report.txt, alongside the tarball, flagging any
        NEW COLUMNS / REMOVED COLUMNS explicitly so a human reviews and
        signs off on schema changes even when every shared column's
        values matched -- read this report before trusting a rebuilt
        package for anything beyond local testing.
   Override --sample/--expected-output to verify against a different
   example instead of (or in addition to) TA002_IR_Swap.

5. INSTALL
   The script copies the tarball (and its diff-report.txt) straight
   into external/ore/packages/ -- no separate manual copy step. Pass
   --no-install to build+verify without touching this directory (e.g.
   to inspect the package first with --keep-staging).

6. UPDATE THE COMPUTE APP SEED (if this replaces the seeded version)
   projects/ores.sql/populate/compute/compute_ore_app_seed.sql seeds
   the `ore` compute app's engine_version and package_uri
   (/api/v1/storage/compute/packages/ore/<version>/ore-<version>-x64-linux.tar.gz)
   for the x64-linux platform. The packaging script does NOT update
   this automatically -- deciding whether a new package replaces the
   seeded default (vs. being added as an additional version) is a
   product/deployment decision, not something to infer from a build.

7. COMMIT
   Commit the new tarball + its diff-report.txt + this directory's
   updated manifest.json together. Never hand-edit an existing
   tarball's contents -- rerun the script and get a new one; the
   RPATH/manifest/library-set are all derived, not hand-maintained.
